{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Treat the increment as a change to an existing Spring XD-style Java codebase, preserving established module, admin UI, shell, and deployment conventions.",
    "Fix U1 by tracing the admin UI request through authorization, job creation, and server-side exception handling, and expose an actionable error response while preserving role-based authorization semantics.",
    "Implement explicit partition count as validated module or stream configuration that is propagated to the Kafka producer or routing component without requiring broker-side changes.",
    "Implement dynamic Kafka partition subscription using Kafka consumer subscription and rebalance mechanisms, with configuration-driven topic or partition discovery rather than manual consumer assignment.",
    "Implement HDFS Syncable writes through the Hadoop filesystem APIs, flushing and syncing data when the option is enabled while retaining the existing behavior by default.",
    "Implement the HDFS filename option as a backward-compatible configuration switch: the existing temporary in-use suffix remains the default, while direct filename writes are used when explicitly enabled.",
    "Implement Maven and Gradle custom-module installation as build targets that package the module fragment and invoke the existing module upload or registration API.",
    "Version custom modules using explicit module version metadata and version-aware installation and lookup, while retaining compatibility with unversioned or existing module references.",
    "Certify against PHD 3.0 by updating compatibility configuration and dependencies as needed, running the supported test suites, and fixing incompatibilities discovered during validation.",
    "Use automated unit tests for configuration and business logic, integration tests for Kafka and HDFS behavior, and regression tests for the admin UI and custom-module workflows.",
    "Document new configuration properties, build targets, versioning behavior, operational limitations, and upgrade or migration guidance."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing repository, build, test infrastructure, and development environments are available and can be built locally.",
    "The specification represents one increment covering all eight user stories; no separate product-management or requirements-analysis phase is required beyond technical interpretation.",
    "U1 is a reproducible defect in the existing admin UI or server workflow, and the intended authorization rules are that ROLE_CREATE and ROLE_ADMIN can create jobs.",
    "The admin UI, shell, and server use existing APIs that can be extended without a complete redesign or database migration.",
    "Kafka and HDFS dependencies are already present in the codebase, and compatible local or test-cluster environments can be provisioned without external infrastructure procurement.",
    "Dynamic partition subscription means discovering and subscribing to partitions or partition patterns added after initial startup, with normal Kafka consumer rebalancing; exact real-time latency guarantees are not required.",
    "Syncable HDFS writes can be implemented using the available Hadoop filesystem API and do not require changes to HDFS itself.",
    "Custom module upload endpoints and module-fragment packaging conventions already exist; the work adds automation and version metadata rather than creating a new artifact repository.",
    "PHD 3.0 certification is limited to compatibility testing and required source, dependency, or configuration fixes, not certification of every supported deployment topology.",
    "One developer performs implementation, testing, documentation, and integration work; estimates are work-hours and exclude elapsed waiting time for external reviews or infrastructure availability.",
    "No major redesign, security audit, performance benchmark campaign, or upgrade of the entire Spring Framework baseline is required."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository setup and technical analysis",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing architecture, build files, module conventions, admin UI and shell workflows, Kafka and HDFS integrations, custom-module lifecycle, and PHD compatibility matrix. Establish local build and test baselines and refine implementation points for all user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Admin UI job-creation defect fix",
      "activity_description": "Reproduce U1 for ROLE_CREATE and ROLE_ADMIN, trace the request and authorization path, correct the defect, improve server-side error propagation or logging, and add regression coverage for UI/API job creation and role handling.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Explicit partition count configuration",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration parsing, validation, propagation, and runtime handling for an explicit partition count, including invalid-value behavior and compatibility with existing default partition behavior. Add unit and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Dynamic Kafka partition subscription",
      "activity_description": "Extend the Kafka source module to discover and subscribe to dynamic partitions, handle consumer rebalance and assignment changes safely, preserve offset and error behavior, and test partition additions and message consumption.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "HDFS Syncable write option",
      "activity_description": "Add an opt-in HDFS sink configuration for Syncable writes, implement the required flush and synchronization behavior, handle failure and close paths, preserve the default mode, and add unit and integration coverage.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "HDFS direct filename option",
      "activity_description": "Add an opt-in configuration that disables the temporary inUseSuffix and writes directly to the configured filename. Cover interactions with Syncable writes, restart and failure behavior, existing rename logic, and backward compatibility.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Maven and Gradle custom-module upload targets",
      "activity_description": "Implement Maven and Gradle targets for packaging and uploading custom module fragments through the existing installation interface, including parameter handling, authentication or endpoint configuration, failure reporting, and build-script tests or examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Custom-module versioning",
      "activity_description": "Add version metadata and version-aware module registration, lookup, installation, and upgrade behavior. Ensure old unversioned modules remain usable where possible and add tests for multiple versions and seamless rollout scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "PHD 3.0 compatibility certification",
      "activity_description": "Prepare the PHD 3.0 test environment, update dependency and compatibility settings, execute core and integration test suites, diagnose and fix compatibility issues, and record certification results and known limitations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature regression and integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete regression suite and targeted end-to-end scenarios across admin job creation, Kafka partition routing and discovery, HDFS failure recovery, custom-module upload and version upgrades, including test cleanup and defect correction from test findings.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation and operational guidance",
      "activity_description": "Document new properties, defaults, examples, Kafka subscription behavior, HDFS Syncable and filename semantics, Maven and Gradle targets, custom-module versioning, PHD 3.0 compatibility, upgrade notes, and troubleshooting information.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Packaging, CI integration, and release preparation",
      "activity_description": "Update build and CI configuration, verify reproducible packaging, include migration or configuration metadata, perform final clean-build validation, review changes for release readiness, and assemble the increment release notes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 432
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the increment as a change to an existing Spring XD-style Java codebase, preserving established module, admin UI, shell, and deployment conventions.

Fix U1 by tracing the admin UI request through authorization, job creation, and server-side exception handling, and expose an actionable error response while preserving role-based authorization semantics.
Implement explicit partition count as validated module or stream configuration that is propagated to the Kafka producer or routing component without requiring broker-side changes.

Implement dynamic Kafka partition subscription using Kafka consumer subscription and rebalance mechanisms, with configuration-driven topic or partition discovery rather than manual consumer assignment.
Implement HDFS Syncable writes through the Hadoop filesystem APIs, flushing and syncing data when the option is enabled while retaining the existing behavior by default.

Implement the HDFS filename option as a backward-compatible configuration switch: the existing temporary in-use suffix remains the default, while direct filename writes are used when explicitly enabled.
Implement Maven and Gradle custom-module installation as build targets that package the module fragment and invoke the existing module upload or registration API.
Version custom modules using explicit module version metadata and version-aware installation and lookup, while retaining compatibility with unversioned or existing module references.
Certify against PHD 3.0 by updating compatibility configuration and dependencies as needed, running the supported test suites, and fixing incompatibilities discovered during validation.
Use automated unit tests for configuration and business logic, integration tests for Kafka and HDFS behavior, and regression tests for the admin UI and custom-module workflows.
Document new configuration properties, build targets, versioning behavior, operational limitations, and upgrade or migration guidance.
assumptions: The existing repository, build, test infrastructure, and development environments are available and can be built locally.
The specification represents one increment covering all eight user stories; no separate product-management or requirements-analysis phase is required beyond technical interpretation.
U1 is a reproducible defect in the existing admin UI or server workflow, and the intended authorization rules are that ROLE_CREATE and ROLE_ADMIN can create jobs.
The admin UI, shell, and server use existing APIs that can be extended without a complete redesign or database migration.
Kafka and HDFS dependencies are already present in the codebase, and compatible local or test-cluster environments can be provisioned without external infrastructure procurement.

Dynamic partition subscription means discovering and subscribing to partitions or partition patterns added after initial startup, with normal Kafka consumer rebalancing; exact real-time latency guarantees are not required.
Syncable HDFS writes can be implemented using the available Hadoop filesystem API and do not require changes to HDFS itself.
Custom module upload endpoints and module-fragment packaging conventions already exist; the work adds automation and version metadata rather than creating a new artifact repository.
PHD 3.0 certification is limited to compatibility testing and required source, dependency, or configuration fixes, not certification of every supported deployment topology.
One developer performs implementation, testing, documentation, and integration work; estimates are work-hours and exclude elapsed waiting time for external reviews or infrastructure availability.
No major redesign, security audit, performance benchmark campaign, or upgrade of the entire Spring Framework baseline is required.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing architecture, build files, module conventions, admin UI and shell workflows, Kafka and HDFS integrations, custom-module lifecycle, and PHD compatibility matrix. Establish local build and test baselines and refine implementation points for all user stories.

Reproduce U1 for ROLE_CREATE and ROLE_ADMIN, trace the request and authorization path, correct the defect, improve server-side error propagation or logging, and add regression coverage for UI/API job creation and role handling.

Add configuration parsing, validation, propagation, and runtime handling for an explicit partition count, including invalid-value behavior and compatibility with existing default partition behavior. Add unit and integration tests.

Extend the Kafka source module to discover and subscribe to dynamic partitions, handle consumer rebalance and assignment changes safely, preserve offset and error behavior, and test partition additions and message consumption.

Add an opt-in HDFS sink configuration for Syncable writes, implement the required flush and synchronization behavior, handle failure and close paths, preserve the default mode, and add unit and integration coverage.

Add an opt-in configuration that disables the temporary inUseSuffix and writes directly to the configured filename. Cover interactions with Syncable writes, restart and failure behavior, existing rename logic, and backward compatibility.

activities.activity_name: Maven and Gradle custom-module upload targets
activities.activity_description: Implement Maven and Gradle targets for packaging and uploading custom module fragments through the existing installation interface, including parameter handling, authentication or endpoint configuration, failure reporting, and build-script tests or examples.

Add version metadata and version-aware module registration, lookup, installation, and upgrade behavior. Ensure old unversioned modules remain usable where possible and add tests for multiple versions and seamless rollout scenarios.

Prepare the PHD 3.0 test environment, update dependency and compatibility settings, execute core and integration test suites, diagnose and fix compatibility issues, and record certification results and known limitations.

Run the complete regression suite and targeted end-to-end scenarios across admin job creation, Kafka partition routing and discovery, HDFS failure recovery, custom-module upload and version upgrades, including test cleanup and defect correction from test findings.

Document new properties, defaults, examples, Kafka subscription behavior, HDFS Syncable and filename semantics, Maven and Gradle targets, custom-module versioning, PHD 3.0 compatibility, upgrade notes, and troubleshooting information.

activities.activity_name: Packaging, CI integration, and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Update build and CI configuration, verify reproducible packaging, include migration or configuration metadata, perform final clean-build validation, review changes for release readiness, and assemble the increment release notes.
